standard_prerequisites.name: Conditions, the forcing question, forcing and the effectiveness of the forcing question
standard_prerequisites.statement: A condition is a triple of a colouring constrained by a computable bounding function, a finite stem and an infinite reservoir computing a fixed set D, with the defining properties (a) and (b); the forcing question holds for a condition and a formula when every relation of the bounded space admits a finite free block in the reservoir that makes the formula true on the enlarged stem, and the lemma immediately preceding this one shows that question to be equivalent to a first-order statement about a single level of bounded progressive functions. Forcing for a condition is the property that every sufficiently generic filter containing it makes the formula true of the induced set. The author's own definitions and that preceding lemma are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the specification of the forcing question: it is what licenses reading the first-order question as a statement about extensions that force the formula or its negation, and it is invoked by the diagonalisation that follows.

core_obligations: First direction: assume the forcing question holds; by the effectiveness lemma fix a level and take a reservoir stabilising that level while still avoiding the cone of the fixed set, so that its limit colouring is bounded and progressive and therefore admits a finite free block making the formula true on the enlarged stem (source line 1229).

Continue the first direction: that block is free for the limit colouring, so appending it to the stem preserves property (b); shrinking the reservoir once more restores property (a) and keeps the cone avoided, which makes the enlarged triple a valid extension (source lines 1230-1231).

Conclude the first direction from the choice of the block: the extension forces the formula, because every sufficiently generic filter containing it must meet the condition that witnesses the formula (source line 1231, last sentence).

Second direction: assume the forcing question fails, so some relation of the bounded space has no free block making the formula true; thin the colouring by adjoining the values of that relation outside the stem, which keeps the new colouring below the old one, makes every free set for it free for the relation, and keeps it bounded and progressive (source line 1233).

Conclude the second direction by contradiction: the thinned triple is again a valid extension with property (b) inherited and property (a) restored; if an extension of it made the formula true then the stem of that extension would be free for the thinned colouring, hence free for the relation, and the part added to the stem would be a free block for the relation making the formula true, which is exactly what the chosen relation forbids (source line 1235).

proof_roadmap.step: First direction: use the effectiveness lemma to reach a stabilising reservoir whose limit colouring admits a witnessing block.
First direction: preserve property (b) by the free block, restore property (a) by shrinking, and read off forcing.
Second direction: thin the colouring along the relation that witnesses the failure of the question.
Second direction: any extension making the formula true would produce a forbidden free block, so the thinned condition forces the negation.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:fs-forcing-question-spec（源 1221-1227 行，证明 1228-1236 行）：若 p ⊩ φ(G) 则存在 p 的扩张 forcing φ(G)；若 p ⊮ φ(G) 则存在扩张 forcing ¬φ(G)（φ 为 Σ^0_1）。关键操作不是例行核验：正向要把「forcing question 成立」经 §6 的效力引理变成「存在 k 与稳定 [0,k] 的 Y₀ 使极限着色 g_{k,Y₀} 有见证 ρ」，再用 property (b) 保持引理接纳 ρ、用 property (a) 保持引理收缩储库，才拼出合法扩张并读出 forcing（1229-1231 行）；反向要造**变薄着色** f̂(s)=f(s)∪(g_R(s)∖σ)：必须验证 f̂ ≤ f、f̂-free 蕴含 g_R-free、f̂ 仍 constrained 且 progressive，再把反证走到底——若某扩张使 φ(τ) 成立，则由 property (b) 得 τ 是 f̂-free、于是 ρ=τ∖σ 是 g_R-free 且使 φ 成立，与 g_R 的取法矛盾（1233、1235 行）。难点在于第二方向要把「使公式成立」这一性质通过 free 性在各层着色之间搬运；原文位置在证明的 1229、1230-1231、1233、1235 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:fs-forcing-question-spec at source lines 1221-1227 together with its proof at source lines 1228-1236, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

The definition of the forcing question is retained complete, from its opening marker at line 1196 through its closing marker at line 1199; the first revision cut the span one line short and the assembler rightly refused to close the environment, so this revision carries the corrected span.

The retained preamble is the lane's shared slice for this source, now 137 lines: it carries the authors' macro block together with the three calligraphic letter macros that sit between the macro block and the theorem declarations, which this lemma's statement needs for the space of relations.

Two context spans carry the notions the retained statement speaks about: the definition of the forcing question at lines 1196-1199 and the definition of forcing for a condition at line 1218. Both are context, not counted units, and neither overlaps the counted interval. They are deliberately kept out of the interval handed to the gate, because that interval is meant to be the counted unit itself and the gate's label guard refuses an interval that swallows other labelled environments.

The retained proof names four lemmas of the same section at source lines 1121-1125, 1144-1147, 1162-1167 and 1201-1204, each counted by a separate card of this lane. All four are declared as non-load-bearing navigation pointers with the article's own section-wise numbers 6.16, 6.18, 6.20 and 6.23, counted over the numbered environments of section 6; none of their proofs is reproduced and no bibliography is needed because the retained spans contain no citation.

The second direction of the proof introduces a thinned colouring and checks four properties of it in one paragraph, then argues by contradiction through the defining property (b); all of that is the author's own argument and is retained line for line.
